research_scope: Source-free whole-formulation-anchored review of shared prerequisite identities; no source/definition mutation, no parent-definition equivalence, no freeze or gate change.

aliases.reason: The Cohen-ring source says the maximal ideal is generated by a prime integer p, hence is the principal ideal (p). The prime-element and principal-ideal-domain sources use the same one-generator ideal construction. Being the image of a prime integer and generating the unique maximal ideal are additional source-specific conditions, not new principal-ideal definitions.

The scheme source says each point has a neighborhood isomorphic to Spec(R) with its structure sheaf; the affine-scheme source is a locally ringed space isomorphic to Spec(R) with that same structure sheaf. Both use the canonical ringed-space sheaf O_Spec(R), locally represented on distinguished opens D(f) by R_f; locality of affine charts remains specific to the scheme definition.

The filtered-colimit-of-étale-algebras source uses an R-algebra isomorphism A≅colim A_i; the finite-presentation source uses R-algebra isomorphism with a polynomial quotient. Both require an invertible unital homomorphism commuting with structure maps from R. Étaleness, filteredness and the selected codomain are properties of the parent statements, not of the isomorphism prerequisite.

The essentially-finite-type ring map source says S is R-isomorphic to a localization T^{-1}A; the finite-presentation source says S is R-isomorphic to a finite polynomial quotient. Both employ the same isomorphism notion in the category of unital R-algebras. Localizing, finite generation and quotient presentation stay as separate source hypotheses.
